one_liner: Otter.ai has a REST public API with self-generated bearer API keys, but it's Enterprise-only and requires account-manager enablement; an official OAuth MCP server exists (mcp.otter.ai).
auth_notes: Public API uses bearer API keys created at Integrations → Developer (limit 2 per user). The MCP server uses OAuth for end users but is not a developer-registerable OAuth API.
access_notes: Public API is stated as available for Enterprise workspaces; if not visible, contact your Otter account manager. The pages fetched do not show self-serve signup or a trial for Enterprise, so the draft's claims about contact-sales and a 100-user minimum are not verified here.
blocker_notes: API access requires an Enterprise plan and enablement via an Otter account manager. The official MCP server is OAuth-based with 3 tools (get user info, search, fetch), but it is not a general developer API.
